question: Does the compiled private Codex execution module create, run, resume, stream and clean up native turns with the outcomes it claims, holding one writer per validated session and never resending after uncertain entry?

scenarios.X4: ownership release on host-attested exit across app-servers
scenarios.X5: same-process reopen after close is busy

pinnedFields: X1 snapshot, event kinds, native methods, turnStartedSeen, usageSeen and native usage; X2 resumeTurns; X5 unsubscribe, reopen and afterReopen; X6 completion and inferenceBeforeExit; X7 snapshot, completion, error code and turn events; X8 error notification presence and willRetry. Outcomes, counts, booleans and native-reported usage only: no ID, path, timestamp or hash is pinned. Once outcome is non-null, execution-proof.mjs fails on any other pinned value.

native.detail: Recorded from identical pinned objects on linux/arm64 (coordinator, local) and linux/x64 (CI) at 08810ca, with harness and X1-X9 all true on both. Natively observed on both: thread/tokenUsage/updated delivers six-field total and last usage, turn/started arrives (opaque), an invalid UserInput turn/start gets error -32600 and maps to rejected, thread/unsubscribe does not unload (X5 reopen busy) and the error notification reports willRetry false. Usage was then promoted to qualified, so the pin differs from the 08810ca reports only in X1.usage.evidence (unqualified to qualified); CI reruns x64 against this pin on every head, and arm64 is rerun by the coordinator. Every later run fails on any other pinned value.

scope: Synthetic Linux homes and a loopback Responses service only. Not macOS, live providers, cross-process admission, uncooperative external writers or approvals.
